text:
A muscle fibre relaxes when calcium ions are actively pumped back into the sarcoplasmic reticulum, removing them from troponin so tropomyosin can block the myosin-binding sites on actin and prevent cross-bridge formation. The fibre then returns to its resting length passively. Note: the claim that skeletal muscle fibres are signaled by sensory neurons bypassing the neuromuscular junction is incorrect—skeletal muscle contraction is triggered by somatic motor neurons at the neuromuscular junction.
CONFIDENCE: 95
